reason: I came in expecting to redeploy cash and the research argued the other way, so I am standing still. The book is three sessions old (entered 09-30) at 70% gross / 30% cash, NAV +5.48% vs SPY +3.80%, and every leg is doing what I bought it for: CRDO +12.2% (Q2 revenue $479M, +114.7% YoY, EPS $1.20 vs $1.17), ALAB -1.6% but with revenue +104% YoY and Scorpio-X in volume production ahead of schedule, HOOD flat with BTIG/KBW flagging better-than-expected Q3 metrics, September crypto volume the highest since February, event contracts +17% MoM, the Treasury trustee mandate for Trump Accounts, and sell-side targets clustered at $134-150 against a $112 mark. Nothing in the three theses broke, so there is nothing to replace. The temptation was the 10-02 payrolls miss, which cut October hike odds to near zero and would normally weaken the hiking-cycle rationale behind my 30% cash. But the tape says the opposite: the 10-year closed at 5.27% on 10-02, the highest since 2002, and it rose THROUGH the soft print. That is a fiscal and term-premium selloff, not a growth-expectations one, and it is the single worst configuration for long-duration small/mid-cap growth multiples: discount rates climbing for reasons monetary easing will not fix, while the labor data that would normally rescue earnings is itself softening. Rate risk did not leave the book, it changed hands. So the de-risk I did last week is more justified today than it was when I did it, and 30% cash at 4% is a position I am actively choosing, not neglect. Against that, replacing has a specific cost beyond the 2bps: re-entry resets my fills and the stop cushions underneath them. CRDO's stop sits at ~146 off a 194.79 fill; re-entering near 219 drags it to ~165 on a name whose 52-week range is 86-309, converting a survivable drawdown into a stop-out. I will not pay that to buy a stock I already own 12% higher than I bought it. Adding a fourth AI-infrastructure leg is also the wrong diversification: CRDO and ALAB are already 48% of the book on one factor (hyperscaler connectivity capex, with CRDO's top three customers at ~88% of revenue), and cash is currently the only thing in here that is not that trade. I also note ALAB now carries two-sided sell-side flow (Northland cut to Market Perform on valuation, Barclays on UALink share) but its driver is shipped revenue, and the Nov 10 print, not an analyst note, settles it. Catalysts are all ahead of me and none need a new position: ALAB Nov 10, CRDO Dec 2, HOOD's Q3 print, plus live S&P 500 inclusion optionality in ALAB. Holding is the active call this week.
